mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: certified copy from the Hong Kong Companies Registry followed by Hong Kong SAR Apostille certificate. Non-Hague route: notarization followed by consular legalization at the relevant PRC embassy or consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive and must never be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notarial certification of the certificate and then Hong Kong SAR Apostille certificate. Non-Hague route: notarization and then consular legalization at the PRC consulate with no apostille step.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney approving the WFOE formation and authorising the local agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Must be notarized by a Hong Kong notary public and thereafter either apostilled (where the notary is in a Hague Apostille Convention state) or consular-legalized (where the notary is in a non-member state); the two pathways are parallel and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the Hong Kong holding company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (registered copy) or board-certified true copy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague route: notarized copy plus Hong Kong SAR Apostille. Non-Hague route: notarized copy plus PRC consular legalization. Use one route only; never add consular legalization to an apostilled document or vice versa.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter from the Hong Kong holding company's principal bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank in Hong Kong where the holding company maintains its account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original wet-ink bank letter must be notarized and then either apostilled (if the bank certificate originates in an Apostille Convention jurisdiction) or consular-legalized (if it originates in a non-member state); no sequential combination of apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, senior managers and authorized signatories must be screened against the United Nations Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU and UK consolidated lists, and the PRC domestic money-laundering risk list. Enhanced due diligence must identify politically exposed persons (PEPs), their immediate family members and close associates, using reputable commercial databases and official registers. Any match must trigger escalation to the AML compliance officer, source-of-wealth verification, transaction monitoring, and negative news screening. Thresholds and risk scoring must follow FATF recommendations and PBOC customer due diligence rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS) / State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Name Clearance Module
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Chinese company name must follow the statutory four-tier structure: (1) administrative division; (2) distinctive trade name; (3) industry or business description; and (4) legal form '有限公司'. If a foreign language name is used, it must be a phonetic or semantic transliteration of the Chinese name and must not be misleading. Pinyin may be registered as the romanized form only when no Chinese-language name conflicts; the registration authority may reject any name mixing Latin letters, Arabic numerals, or non-standard symbols.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 15 working days after a formal rejection, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the original SAMR registration department, enclosing the rejection notice, the proposed amended name, and a legal explanation of each prohibited or sensitive token. If rejected again, the applicant may seek administrative reconsideration from the next higher SAMR authority within 60 days of the second rejection, or directly file an administrative lawsuit in the competent people's court within six months. The appeal must also address potential confusion with prior rights holders and include a search report from NECIPS.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Under PRC regulations, a WFOE must have a registered office address that is capable of receiving official correspondence and legal documents. A virtual office or commercial mailbox is generally not accepted by municipal SAMR and tax authorities for operating enterprises with ongoing business substance; however, some licensed incubators and fintech pilot zones allow a 'cluster registration' or virtual address for SaaS and software companies. Banks and tax bureaus may treat a mail-only address as a red flag for VAT invoice issuance and corporate account opening. Therefore, a physical office lease or an approved incubator address with staffed occupancy and mail handling is strongly recommended for the PropTech/real-estate SaaS industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 25-35% annual probability for a newly incorporated WFOE using a virtual or incubator address; below 10% for a fully physical leased office. Checklist: (1) prominent Chinese name plates at the registered address; (2) valid lease contract, rent receipts and property tax proof; (3) business license and tax registration notice displayed; (4) presence of employees, computers and operational records; (5) corporate seal and accounting materials; (6) utility bills in company name; (7) bank settlement records matching declared turnover; (8) no contradiction with NECIPS registered business scope. Municipal tax bureau and SAMR conduct 'double random, one public' inspections and may revoke registration if the office is found vacated.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) of Hong Kong, particularly Sections 67 (Incorporation), 68 (Application for Incorporation), 112 (Registered Office), 113 (Appointment of Directors), 114 (Appointment of Company Secretary), and 121 (Share Capital).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (under the Companies Ordinance, Cap. 622)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Form NNC1 (Application for Incorporation of a Company) and Articles of Association (Model Articles or Custom Articles)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong law does not impose a minimum paid-up capital requirement. The company may be incorporated with a nominal share capital of HKD 1.00 (or any amount) and shares may be issued at par or premium. No escrow or blocked account is required.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED (the 'Company'), held at [Registered Office Address], Hong Kong, on [Date] at [Time]. PRESENT: [Director 1], [Director 2], [Director 3] (if applicable). The Chairman noted that the Company was incorporated under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) on [Date of Incorporation] and that the following resolutions were proposed and unanimously passed. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the allotment and issue of [Number] ordinary shares of HKD [Par Value] each, at par, to the subscriber(s) as set out in the Statement of Capital filed with the Companies Registry, be and is hereby ratified and confirmed. The Chairman confirmed that the consideration for such shares has been fully received in cash or in kind as per the subscription agreements. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED that the Company open and maintain bank accounts with [Bank Name] and that the following persons be and are hereby authorized to operate such accounts, singly or jointly as specified: [Director 1], [Director 2], [Company Secretary]. The bank is authorized to honor all cheques, drafts, and electronic instructions signed by any two of the authorized signatories. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be established at [Full Address], Hong Kong, and that the Company Secretary be instructed to file the necessary notice with the Companies Registry. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [Director 1] be appointed as the Managing Director, [Director 2] as the Finance Director, and [Name] as the Company Secretary, each to hold office until the next annual general meeting or until earlier resignation or removal. The Company Secretary is authorized to file all statutory returns and maintain the statutory registers. 5. GENERAL AUTHORITY: RESOLVED that the directors be authorized to execute all documents, open bank accounts, and take all actions necessary to give effect to these resolutions. The Chairman declared the meeting adjourned.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong (online via e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Registry's Cyber Search Centre to ensure the proposed company name is not identical to an existing entity or trademark. Submit an application for name reservation (Form NNC1 includes name approval) or use the 'Company Name Check' service. The name must end with 'Limited' and must not be offensive or imply illegal activities. If the name is approved, proceed to incorporation. If the name is rejected, select an alternative and resubmit. The entire process is online and requires a valid Hong Kong address for the registered office.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all subscribers (passport or HKID)
Proof of registered office address (e.g., tenancy agreement)
Details of proposed directors and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, the applicant may file an appeal with the Companies Registry within 14 days, or simply choose a new name and resubmit. The registry will provide a reason for rejection, and the applicant can rectify any issues (e.g., similarity) by amending the name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Submission of Incorporation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong (e-Registry or physical counter)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Incorporation Form NNC1, which includes the company name, registered office address, details of directors, company secretary, and share capital. Attach the Articles of Association (either Model Articles or custom articles). All subscribers must sign the form and articles. Submit the application online via the e-Registry portal or in person at the Companies Registry. Pay the prescribed fee (HKD 1,720 for incorporation and HKD 1,720 for business registration certificate, total approx. USD 440). The registry will review the application for compliance with the Companies Ordinance. If all documents are in order, the Certificate of Incorporation will be issued.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Form NNC3) for each director
Consent to act as company secretary (Form NNC3)
Copy of lease or proof of registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registry will issue a notice specifying deficiencies. The applicant must rectify within 14 days by submitting amended forms or additional documents. If the application is suspended, the applicant may request a review or appeal to the Companies Registry's internal review board. Failure to cure may result in rejection, but the applicant can reapply with corrected information.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department (Business Registration Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful incorporation, the Companies Registry issues a Certificate of Incorporation. Simultaneously, the Business Registration Office (under the Inland Revenue Department) issues a Business Registration Certificate. The company must display both certificates at its registered office. The Business Registration Certificate must be renewed annually. The company must also obtain a company seal (if desired) and open a corporate bank account. The incorporation is effective from the date of the certificate.
required_dossiers: List of directors and company secretary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Business Registration Certificate is delayed, the company may operate temporarily with a receipt of application. If the certificate is denied, the company may appeal to the Inland Revenue Department. For the Certificate of Incorporation, there is no remedy as it is issued upon compliance; any errors must be corrected via a court order.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department, and Commercial Banks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of incorporation, the company must appoint a company secretary (if not already appointed) and file the notice of appointment with the Companies Registry. The registered office address must be filed. The company must also open a corporate bank account by providing the Certificate of Incorporation, Business Registration Certificate, Articles, and board resolution authorizing the account. The bank will conduct due diligence and may require additional documents such as proof of beneficial ownership. The company must also hold its first board meeting to adopt the resolutions as per the pro-forma resolution. All statutory registers (members, directors, charges) must be maintained at the registered office.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of directors and shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application, the company may apply to another bank or provide additional documentation. If the Companies Registry queries the appointment of officers, the company must file the correct forms. For any non-compliance, the company may be subject to penalties; remedies include filing late returns with a fee and applying for relief from the Registrar.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA); electronic filings are submitted through the STA National Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax) online portal. Export-related customs and tax information is exchanged through the China International Trade Single Window operated by the General Administration of Customs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE), the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) issues an 18-digit Unified Social Credit Code (USCC) on the Business Licence; this USCC is the sole statutory tax identification number for VAT, corporate income tax, and local surtaxes. Within 30 calendar days after business licence issuance, the WFOE must complete post-registration tax formalities through the e-Tax portal: authenticate the legal representative and shareholders, upload the articles of association, choose the accounting/fiscal year and filing frequency, register its bank deposit account with the PRC tax authority, declare its taxpayer classification (small-scale or general VAT taxpayer), and apply for the electronic invoice quota and tax-control e-invoice system. No separate physical TIN card is issued. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a mainland permanent establishment (for example the HK parent) must additionally complete non-resident enterprise tax registration in the e-Tax system using its home-jurisdiction tax ID and register a PRC withholding agent or payer for China-source dividends, interest, royalties, and service fees.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None; China does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch entity elections. A WFOE is mandatorily treated as a PRC resident enterprise subject to enterprise income tax on worldwide income. Available elections are limited to preferential tax treatments (e.g., small and low-profit enterprise rate, R&D super deduction, accelerated depreciation) and do not alter the entity-level tax classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration is triggered when the previous 12-month taxable turnover exceeds RMB 5,000,000; a newly established WFOE must obtain tax registration immediately upon formation regardless of turnover and will be treated as a small-scale taxpayer until the threshold is exceeded unless it elects general taxpayer status.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China mandates the use of the STA unified national electronic invoice platform and tax-control invoice system. VAT invoices (including fully digitalised electronic invoices) must be issued through STA-approved tax-control software, are transmitted in real time to the tax authority, carry an anti-counterfeiting tax-control code, and are reconciled electronically with the enterprise's VAT filing. No private third-party clearance API is recognised for statutory VAT invoicing; integration with the e-Tax portal and the digital tax-control environment is mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies to goods actually exported from mainland China after customs clearance and to qualifying cross-border services, including software, information technology, and related technology/SaaS services, where the service recipient is located outside mainland China, the service is fully consumed outside mainland China, payment is received from overseas, and the WFOE retains evidence satisfying the STA's cross-border taxable services rules. For goods, zero-rating is claimed on the export VAT return with the customs export declaration; for services, the taxpayer may claim zero-rating or VAT exemption and must maintain a separate input VAT allocation for the zero-rated supply chain.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Goods Declaration for Exportation) generated through the China International Trade Single Window and matched with the exporter's VAT filing; mandatory for physical goods exports.
Transport document proving actual export movement from mainland China: Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international courier/cross-border postal consignment note.

Bank foreign-exchange inward remittance notice or cross-border RMB settlement receipt matched with SAFE's Trade Foreign Exchange Monitoring System (the PRC equivalent of an export collection/payment verification record).

For zero-rated SaaS services: signed cross-border service contract, overseas recipient business registration evidence, service delivery/usage logs demonstrating consumption outside mainland China, and the overseas payment receipt; no customs goods declaration is applicable to pure services.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA cross-audits zero-rating claims against Customs and SAFE data, bank receipts, service contracts, and technology logs. If the required documentation is missing, fraudulent, or untimely, the tax authority reassesses the supply at the applicable VAT rate (6% for SaaS services or 13% for goods), charges a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and may impose administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax. Deliberate export zero-rating/invoice fraud triggers unlimited retroactive clawback, suspension or revocation of export-tax-refund qualification, and criminal liability for tax fraud. Negligent documentary defects are generally assessable within three to five years, while fraudulent claims have no statute-of-limitations protection.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) through the delegated State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Under mainland China's FX architecture, current account items enjoy managed convertibility: bona fide trade in services and goods can be settled via designated banks on an authenticity-review basis, without central approval, provided contracts, invoices, customs records or service performance evidence are retained. Capital account items remain highly controlled: each injection, M&A, and investment exit must be registered with SAFE and routed through a dedicated capital account. FDI proceeds in a WFOE are treated as registered capital and can be converted to RMB at spot, but the RMB cannot be deployed for speculative stock-market investment, wealth-management products, or unauthorized intercompany loans; it must be applied to the entity's actual operating needs. Export receipts are not subject to an across-the-board mandatory conversion ratio, but they must come onshore and be reconciled with customs/SAFE trade monitoring. Profit remittance is permitted only after statutory annual audit, final corporate income tax settlement, and payment of dividends; banks require audited financials, a board dividend resolution confirming after-tax profits, and proof that the tax bureau has filed the withholding of 10% dividend income tax, making the actual remittance timely and lawful but administratively heavy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export receipts must be collected through a designated FX bank within 180 days of the customs export declaration and matched to SAFE's goods-trade monitoring system. There is no mandatory percentage surrender ratio under normal circumstances; the exporter may retain 100% of export FX in a settlement account, convert to RMB at spot, or use those balances for approved current-account obligations, but every credit and debit must be backed by customs declarations and authentic transaction documents. A/B/C trade classification ratings shape the documentary threshold: B- and C-rated exporters face stricter scrutiny, pre-approval requirements, and reduced timelines.

Multi-Currency Operational Settlement Account with SAFE-linked e-Banking Rails

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is low for a primary onshore treasury rail. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Airwallex, Payoneer, or Stripe Treasury are not licensed domestic commercial banks in the PRC and are legally barred from maintaining a WFOE's sole settlement ledger. SAFE permits only licensed cross-border payment institutions to collect foreign SaaS revenue and remit net funds in RMB after authenticating the underlying software-export contracts. However, domestic payroll, VAT, social insurance, withholding tax, and FX hedging must all flow through a PBOC-regulated commercial bank. Therefore, EMIs should be positioned only as an ancillary receivable-collection accelerator, never as the corporate banking spine.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PBOC-regulated banks require the WFOE's legal representative, or two authorized on-site officers acting under an original notarized and legalized power of attorney, to complete identity verification physically in the bank branch during initial onboarding. Remote consular proxy opening is generally not accepted as a substitute for the statutory interview. If the legal representative is a Hong Kong or other offshore individual, additional passport verification, Hong Kong residency proof, board resolutions, and enhanced scrutiny are mandatory. Some nationwide banks permit a video-call interview only after the branch compliance officer has physically verified all delegate identities and the registered premises, but the strict default remains that at least one person with corporate signatory capacity must appear in person at the named branch.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Holding-company ownership chain terminating in a Hong Kong shell with no transparent nexus to the mainland PropTech operating entity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier must include the Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate, NAR1 annual return, register of members, passports of all directors, a notarized group ownership chart, beneficial ownership declaration, audited Hong Kong holdco financial statements, and a bank reference from the remitting financial institution proving the equity injection is sourced from legitimate accumulated profits or existing shareholder funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Bank compliance red-flag that the declared FDI capital injection exceeds the WFOE's operating scale or lacks commercial rationale for a low-capital SaaS business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an arm's-length group valuation study justifying the capitalization, a five-year WFOE business plan with cash-flow projections, mainland lease and staffing evidence, a PRC certified public accountant capital verification report, the SAFE FDI registration certificate, and board minutes approving the capital injection and specifically linking funds to PropTech platform R&D and licensing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS subscription revenue collected through Stripe and ACH from US and Hong Kong real-estate clients without a demonstrable software-export trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply signed SaaS master agreements and clickwrap licensing terms, billing invoices, software copyright registration certificates, product documentation, server-side user and transaction logs showing customer geography, reconciled Stripe and ACH settlement reports, service delivery sign-offs, and a valid export-service declaration confirming that the activities qualify as software export under PRC cross-border payment rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to a dense web of offshore technology vendors or related suppliers creating sanctions and transfer-pricing exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver vendor due diligence files with UBO declarations, live OFAC/EU/UN and PRC sanctions screening snapshots, signed service-level agreements proving arm's-length pricing, PRC tax withholding receipts and foreign contractor tax payment vouchers, and transfer-pricing documentation showing benchmarking, so the compliance committee can close the round-trip and unrelated-shell-vendor hypotheses.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: First complete SAFE FDI registration and obtain the entity's foreign-exchange registration code. The Hong Kong parent then issues a board resolution and wires equity capital by SWIFT MT103 bank-to-beneficiary through to the WFOE's dedicated FDI foreign-exchange capital account at the chosen tier-1 bank, quoting the SAFE FDI code and transaction purpose 'Overseas Direct Investment - Equity Capital'. The bank screens the credit, updates SAFE's digital registry, and permits spot conversion into RMB only under the actual-use principle. Once the RMB is credited to the WFOE's basic operating account, a PRC certified public accountant issues the capital verification report. The funds may then be deployed only for registered-business purposes such as payroll, office lease, cloud infrastructure, software development, and routine current-account disbursements; unauthorized intercompany loans, investments, and financial-market speculation are prohibited.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For service imports and cross-border operating expenditure, use SWIFT MT103 transfers with full beneficiary KYC, the relevant transaction purpose code, underlying contract, invoice, and Chinese tax withholding proof. For physical goods or hardware procured for PropTech deployment, use an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit or a Documentary Collection (D/P or D/A) routed through the WFOE's advising and confirming bank, with transport documents, inspection certificates, packing lists, and customs declarations attached. All outbound trade disbursements must clear the bank's post-settlement review and be traceable in the goods-trade or service-trade monitoring system, with proper record retention for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD foreign exchange forward subject to demonstrated underlying USD exposure and a SAFE-approved bank derivative facility
Onshore CNY/HKD foreign exchange swap used for matching equity injection, dividend conversion, or trade settlement cash-flow mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swap converting HKD or USD debt-service exposure into CNY cash-flow exposure where an actual external borrowing exists
Vanilla CNY-USD FX options and zero-cost collars limited to hedging forecast SaaS subscription receipts; speculative net open positions are prohibited
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) protection is not permissible onshore for a PRC-resident WFOE; any CNH NDF hedge must be executed in the offshore Hong Kong book of the group holding company

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Form NAR1) - annual return of shares, debentures, members, directors, company secretary, and registered office particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 42 calendar days after the anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing within 42 days to 3 months after anniversary: HK$1,200 (USD 153.85); over 3 months to 6 months: HK$2,400 (USD 307.69); over 6 months to 9 months: HK$3,600 (USD 461.54); over 9 months to 12 months: HK$4,800 (USD 615.38). In addition, each default officer is liable to prosecution fine of up to HK$50,000 (USD 6,410.26) and daily default fine of HK$1,000 (USD 128.21) per day; continued non-compliance can trigger administrative strike-off under Companies Ordinance Cap. 622.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration (BR) Certificate renewal - one-year business registration renewal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before the expiration of the current one-year BR certificate; IRD renewal demand is typically payable within 30 days from the date of the renewal notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a prescribed late-renewal surcharge under Business Registration Ordinance Cap. 310; carrying on business without a valid BR certificate is an offence punishable by fine of up to HK$5,000 (USD 641.03) and imprisonment for one year, and persistent non-renewal will cause the IRD to report the company to the Companies Registry for strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return (Form BIR51) with audited financial statements, tax computation, and supporting schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the IRD issue date of the Profits Tax Return; one additional month is generally allowed for electronic filing through eTax; returns are normally issued in April for companies with 31 December financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is an offence under Inland Revenue Ordinance Cap. 112; on conviction the maximum fine is HK$10,000 (USD 1,282.05) plus additional tax of up to three times the amount of tax undercharged; IRD may issue an estimated assessment with a 10% uplift and institute recovery proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form IR56B) and multiple forms where applicable to directors and employees
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of the IRD issue date; IRD generally issues the return in April each year and requires filing within one month, normally by 1 May, for the tax year ending 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file renders the employer liable to a maximum fine of HK$10,000 (USD 1,282.05) per offence; knowingly furnishing false information may lead to additional tax of up to three times the tax undercharged and imprisonment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Laying of audited financial statements and auditor's report before members (annual general meeting or unanimous written resolution for a private company)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and members; no filing to the Companies Registry unless a copy of a written resolution is distributed to members
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 9 months after the end of the financial year for a private company; the first financial statements must be laid within 18 months of incorporation or within 9 months of the first financial year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Each officer in default is liable to a fine at Level 4, being HK$25,000 (USD 3,205.13), and a continuing daily default fine of HK$700 (USD 89.74) per day for failure to hold the meeting or lay the financial statements before members.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Appointment of a practising certified public accountant as auditor and completion of the annual audit (auditor's report on the financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and members; the signed auditor's report is filed with the IRD as a schedule to the Profits Tax Return and retained for Companies Registry inspection
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The auditor must be appointed before the end of the financial year being audited; the audit report must be completed in time to be laid before members within 9 months after the financial year end and filed with the Profits Tax Return within the PTR deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint or retain an auditor is an offence under Cap. 622; each officer in default is liable to a fine of HK$25,000 (USD 3,205.13) and a daily default fine of HK$700 (USD 89.74); an unqualified audited report is effectively mandatory for the IRD to accept the Profits Tax Return and for the Companies Registry annual return.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual refresh and inspection-readiness of the Register of Significant Controllers and statutory registers; no separate annual UBO filing to the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Companies Registry can inspect on request; law enforcement agencies access the register under the statutory framework; no filing is required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Continuing obligation; register must be updated within 7 days after the company receives notice of any change in significant controllers or relevant particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance is an offence; each defaulting officer is liable to a fine of HK$25,000 (USD 3,205.13) and, where applicable, a further daily default fine of HK$700 (USD 89.74); the Register must be physically located at the registered office or a prescribed place and any change of location must be filed with the Companies Registry.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Hong Kong law imposes no size-based revenue, asset, or headcount threshold for audit exemption. Every Hong Kong-incorporated private company that is not dormant is legally required to appoint one or more certified public accountants (practising) to audit its financial statements annually. An exemption is available only to a dormant company that has applied to the Companies Registry and has had no significant accounting transactions; an operating PropTech SaaS company cannot rely on the exemption. Accordingly, the audit obligation is mandatory for the target entity irrespective of turnover, balance sheet size, employee count, or number of members.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Companies Ordinance Cap. 622; Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA), which are substantially aligned with IFRS; eligible private companies may apply HKFRS for Private Entities (HKFRS-PE) or prepare a simplified financial report in accordance with Part 9 of Cap. 622; the financial statements must give a true and fair view and include the balance sheet, income statement, statement of changes in equity, cash-flow statement, and related notes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not prescribe a 30-day UBO filing to a central registry; instead it operates a continuing Significant Controllers Register (SCR) under Cap. 622. The company must identify each significant controller and send acknowledgment notices; any person who becomes or ceases to be a significant controller must notify the company within 7 days, and the company must update the SCR within 7 days of receiving that notice. Transfers of shares must be reflected in the Register of Members immediately, and any allotment of shares must be reported to the Companies Registry on Form NSC1 within 1 month. The Annual Return (NAR1) annually restates members and their shareholdings as at the anniversary date and serves as the yearly confirmation of the registered ownership, directors, company secretary, and registered office particulars.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Books for board and members
Financial statements and supporting accounting records

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 640 - USD 2,560 (approximately HK$5,000 - HK$20,000) per annum, inclusive of registered office, annual company secretary, and basic corporate maintenance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,600 - USD 8,900 (approximately HK$20,000 - HK$70,000) per annum for a PropTech/SaaS operating entity, depending on transaction volume, number of group entities, intercompany balances, and audit complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% for a certified High and New Technology Enterprise; 5% effective rate for small low-profit enterprises with qualified annual taxable income up to RMB 3 million for tax years 2023-2027; 100% super deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; two-year exemption and three-year 50% reduction (12.5% effective rate) for qualifying software enterprises, including PropTech SaaS platforms; tax loss carryforward generally 5 years, extended to 10 years for HNTEs and qualified technology-oriented small and medium enterprises.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (Corporate Income Tax Annual Return) and associated supporting schedules (A105000, A105080, A106000, A107012, A109000) filed through the electronic tax filing portal (eTax@China / Electronic Tax Bureau) or in-person at the in-charge tax authority.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual settlement return with quarterly provisional returns and prepayments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT returns are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter; the annual return and final tax payment are due by May 31 of the following calendar year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Revenue from sales of goods or provision of services
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report gross SaaS subscription, property data analytics, and real-estate rental screening revenue net of VAT. Non-resident payments for cloud services must be analysed as services or royalties; Chinese-source royalties paid to a non-resident trigger a separate 10% WHT and are not entered here.

Include government grants, asset disposal gains, and FX gains. If the WFOE receives cash from the HK parent without a valid service arrangement, tax authorities may reclassify the amount as taxable other income and demand transfer pricing documentation.
Auto-sum of Lines 1 and 2. Convert non-RMB revenue at the market exchange rate on the realisation date; maintain books in RMB in accordance with PRC GAAP.

Declare direct cloud hosting, data centre, implementation, and platform maintenance costs. Recharges from the HK parent are deductible only if supported by written agreements, evidence of actual service receipt, and an arm's-length price; otherwise add back under transfer pricing adjustment.

Report staff costs, marketing, cloud fees, and interest. Management fees lacking economic substance are non-deductible under CIT Law Article 41; entertainment expenses are limited under the 60% and 5 per mille rules; interest paid to HK related lenders must respect thin-capitalisation and arm's-length rates.

After the statutory deduction lines, show PRC GAAP profit before tax. This figure must reconcile to audited financial statements; foreign exchange or share-based payment differences are adjusted in Schedule A105000, not in the accounting line.

Add back non-deductible penalties, excess entertainment, unsupported HK head-office allocations, and transfer pricing adjustments. Include excessive interest and royalties disallowed under transfer pricing and thin-capitalisation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment decreases / R&D super deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct the 100% additional R&D expense for qualifying PropTech software development, and any tax-exempt dividends received from other PRC resident companies. Do not offset R&D deductions against WHT on future dividends to HK; they are separate tax lines.
Apply statutory loss carryover using Form A106000; maximum five years, or ten years for HNTEs and qualified technology SMEs. Losses cannot be transferred to the HK parent or any foreign affiliate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable rate, CIT payable, prepayments and final balance
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 25% headline rate, 15% if HNTE, or the software enterprise reduced rate. After subtracting quarterly prepayments and foreign tax credits, the net balance is due by May 31. Dividend distributions to the HK parent are not deductible on this return and are separately subject to withholding tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without reasonable cause attracts an administrative fine of up to RMB 10,000 and an order to rectify; unpaid or underpaid tax accrues a daily late-payment surcharge at 0.05% of the overdue amount under Article 32 TAL. Understatement causing tax underpayment is treated as tax evasion under Article 63 TAL, subject to recovery, daily surcharge, and a fine of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax. Criminal tax evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 arises where evaded tax exceeds RMB 50,000 and exceeds 10% of tax payable, with imprisonment of up to 3 years in ordinary cases, or up to 7 years where the amount is huge and constitutes a high percentage; directors and legal representatives may be blacklisted and restricted from travel or exit if tax arrears remain unpaid.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% (withholding income tax under PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law Articles 3 and 37, collected at the time the WFOE distributes a dividend to its non-resident shareholder; the 10% domestic rate applies to dividends paid to the Hong Kong parent if no treaty relief is claimed).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The China-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement reduces the dividend WHT to 5% if the Hong Kong parent is the beneficial owner and directly holds at least 25% of the WFOE's equity capital. To invoke relief, the HK parent must obtain a Hong Kong Tax Residency Certificate from the IRD, complete the Tax Treaty Benefit Claim Information Form under SAT Public Notice 2019 No. 35, and submit a beneficial ownership declaration evidencing board minutes, staff, office premises, decision-making, and investment-holding substance. The WFOE must withhold at 5% only after risk review and must remit the withheld tax within seven days of withholding. A shell HK company without real economic substance will be denied treaty benefits and the full 10% domestic WHT will be assessed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on interest and royalties is 10%; under the China-HK Arrangement, interest and royalties generally attract a 7% WHT cap, subject to beneficial ownership and permanent establishment safeguards. Interest deductibility is further limited by thin-capitalisation (debt-equity ratio of 2:1 for non-financial enterprises) and transfer pricing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared when total intercompany transactions exceed RMB 400 million in a tax year, or when category-specific thresholds are met: tangible property transfers over RMB 200 million, intangible or financial asset transfers over RMB 100 million, or service transactions over RMB 40 million. Master File is required when the multinational group's prior-year consolidated operating revenue exceeds RMB 5.5 billion, or the taxpayer is selected by the tax authority for a transfer pricing investigation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The WFOE must conduct its PropTech development, cloud hosting, client contracting, risk management, and credit screening in China with actual staff and assets. Under SAT Notice 2017 No. 6, DEMPE functions and core income-generating activities (CIGA) must be assessed for intangible-related returns. The Hong Kong parent must have real economic substance in Hong Kong to qualify as beneficial owner; otherwise the Principal Purpose Test under the DTA can deny treaty benefits and Chinese GAAR under CIT Law Article 47 can recharacterise the structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Deliberate Under-declaration of Chinese-source SaaS Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing PropTech subscription and rental-screening fees through the Hong Kong parent or an offshore entity without a substantive service or sub-licence agreement, failing to recognise Chinese-source income, and using false invoices or inflated cloud costs to strip profits from the WFOE.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 63 of the Tax Collection Administration Law and Article 201 of the Criminal Law of PRC; recovery of underpaid tax plus 0.05% daily surcharge, monetary penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax, and criminal fine; imprisonment up to 3 years for ordinary tax evasion or up to 7 years where the amount is huge and accounts for a high percentage of tax payable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, legal representatives, and financial officers who direct or approve the evasion may be jointly and severally liable for the tax and penalties by piercing the corporate veil under PRC Company Law; their personal assets may be used for restitution; exit bans and tax blacklisting are imposed under Article 44 TAL; criminal prosecution can result in imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Treaty Abuse / Shell Company Used to Claim the 5% Dividend WHT Rate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong parent is a shell with no office, employees, business records, or commercial decisions; the WFOE pays dividends to Hong Kong solely to claim the China-HK DTA 5% rate instead of the statutory 10%, while the true controller is in another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law (General Anti-Avoidance Rule), SAT Public Notice 2019 No. 35, and the Principal Purpose Test in the DTA; the tax authority may deny treaty benefits, reimpose 10% WHT, assess underpaid tax, add daily surcharge, and impose a penalty of 50% to 5 times the evaded tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who certify false Tax Residency Certificates or beneficial ownership declarations can be personally liable for the uncollected WHT; they face civil restitution, blacklisting and travel bans, fines, and criminal liability for fraudulent documents and tax evasion, with imprisonment up to 7 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Compliance Failure / Unsupportable Intercompany Charges
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays excessive royalties or management fees to the Hong Kong parent, or operates with a sustained net loss while the group is profitable, without filing a Local File or Master File, without a TP benchmarking study, and without applying an arm's-length pricing method.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 41 and 46 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, SAT Public Notice 2017 No. 6, and Article 63 TAL; tax authorities may make a transfer pricing adjustment, recharacterize payments, disallow deductions, assess additional corporate income tax, and impose daily late-payment surcharge plus documentation penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who intentionally destroy records, fail to maintain TP documentation, or cause the WFOE to underpay taxes expose themselves to piercing of the corporate veil; personal restitution demands, exit bans and blacklisting, personal fines, and criminal prosecution for evasion under Criminal Law Article 201 may follow, including imprisonment terms of up to 7 years.
